findings.evidence: Ch. 6 §6.3.1: "The two-point analytic mean is 0.842 s (0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0; the display above rounds it to 0.84 s). The plotted synthetic stream's exact mean is 0.85 s — the value Fig 6.2 displays."
findings.issue: Arithmetic defect: 0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 = 0.792 + 0.05 = 0.842 s. But the population mixture as described (99% log-normal with median 0.8 s and σ ≈ 0.12, 1% at 5.0 s) has an analytic mean of 0.99 × E[log-normal] + 0.01 × 5.0, where E[log-normal] = exp(μ + σ²/2) = 0.8 × exp(0.0072) ≈ 0.8058, giving ≈ 0.8476 s — not 0.842 s. The book's '0.842 s' is the two-point approximation (treating the log-normal as its median), yet it is labelled 'the two-point analytic mean' while being presented alongside 'the plotted synthetic stream's exact mean is 0.85 s' as if they were both analytic quantities; the 0.85 s sample value is a single draw of N = 10,000 and is draw-dependent exactly as the p99 is later shown to be (p. 99 at 100 stragglers vs 101).
findings.fix_instruction: State three distinct quantities: (a) the two-point median-substitution approximation 0.842 s; (b) the analytic mixture mean 0.99 × 0.8·exp(σ²/2) + 0.05 ≈ 0.848 s; (c) the sample mean of this particular draw ≈ 0.85 s, with the same draw-dependence caveat the p99 receives.

findings.evidence: Ch. 6 §6.3.2: "Scenario A [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]: the extra 20 tok/s are produced, but they land in the tail that misses the SLO, so goodput does not grow — goodput is unchanged only at f ≈ 68.6 % (48 ÷ 70)..." and later "the compliant fraction falls from 96% to 94%, goodput is 50×0.96 = 48 vs 70×0.94 = 65.8"
findings.issue: Internal contradiction / prose defect: the paragraph first asserts as its Scenario A conclusion that 'goodput does not grow' and 'goodput is unchanged only at f ≈ 68.6%', then immediately presents Scenario B where goodput rises from 48 to 65.8. The Scenario A framing ('the extra 20 tok/s are produced, but they land in the tail that misses the SLO') is asserted rather than derived, and the derived f ≈ 68.6% contradicts the 94% case in the very next sentence — the text then acknowledges this ('The case the opening claim describes is the third one'), but the opening sentence is left standing as a claim in its own right.
findings.fix_instruction: Restructure the three scenarios so each is introduced with its own f and outcome (f = 68.6% → unchanged; f = 94% → rises; f = 65% → falls) and remove the unqualified opening sentence 'goodput does not grow', replacing it with a pointer to the f that produces it.

findings.evidence: Ch. 6 §6.8: "the peak demands ~18.6× one host's prefill capacity... Hosts were raised from H = 1 to H = 21... the peak prefill oversubscription falls from 18.6× to 51.6 ÷ (21 × 2.77) ≈ 0.9×"
findings.issue: Arithmetic check that does not close cleanly: 51.6 PFLOP/s ÷ (21 hosts × 2.77 PFLOP/s per host) = 51.6 ÷ 58.17 = 0.887 ≈ 0.89, printed as '≈ 0.9×'. The rounding is loose but acceptable; the harder issue is the internal consistency of the per-host sustained capacity: Ch. 8's per-host figure of ~2.77 PFLOP/s comes from 8 × 0.989 PFLOPS × 0.35 = 2.769 PFLOP/s, while Ch. 8's token-rate version of the same capacity is ~19,780 tok/s ÷ 140 GFLOP/token = 2.769 PFLOP/s — consistent. However the mini-case elsewhere (p. 124) states 10 rps '≈ 4.7 host-equivalents' (12.9 ÷ 2.77 = 4.66) and the peak 18.6 (51.6 ÷ 2.77 = 18.63), so the ratios are consistent but the '0.9×' residual is presented without the '≥' / upper-bound qualifier that the same paragraph applies to the 16.2 host-equivalent residual figure ('bound-derived, not measured').
findings.fix_instruction: Carry the same qualifier onto the post-scale figure: print '≈0.89× (an upper bound on the post-cache ratio, before any prefix-cache saving)', so the two residual figures (16.2 host-equivalents and 0.9×) share one status statement.

findings.evidence: Ch 6 (PDF 147): "(The vLLM FP8-KV blog's '54%' is a decode-ITL latency slope, not a memory ratio.)" — untagged. Ch 1 (PDF 31): "is, on this book's reading of that table, a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope, not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient [1P][HYPOTHESIS]. That reading is the book's own, not a vendor-stated interpretation; re-verify it against the post."
findings.issue: Same interpretation carries [1P][HYPOTHESIS] plus an explicit re-verify hedge in Ch 1, but is restated as settled fact with no tag in Ch 6's Architecture Consequence — an epistemic-status regression between chapters on a claim that guides the KV-quantization lever.
findings.fix_instruction: Carry the [1P][HYPOTHESIS] tag and the 'book's own reading, re-verify' hedge into the Ch 6 sentence.

findings.evidence: Three standalone tags with no Axis-1 partner: PDF 142: "— see §6.6 for the conditions under which it pays. [DERIVED] (Source keys: …"; PDF 152: "…reused for a different generation mechanism. [DERIVED]"; PDF 154: "…but that is not the growing autoregressive cache. [DERIVED]".
findings.issue: Violates the book's own rule ("A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes"; "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair"): three bare [DERIVED] tags with no provenance tag.
findings.fix_instruction: Partner each with its Axis-1 tag ([canonical scenario][DERIVED] or [1P][DERIVED], per the claim's actual provenance).

findings.evidence: Rendered figure label: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" (PDF 140). Ch 4 (PDF 104): "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling". Fig 6.2's own caption: "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget".
findings.issue: The figure's annotation labels the 2 s p95 ceiling as 'TTFT budget', contradicting the budget-vs-ceiling distinction the book declares load-bearing and which the figure's own caption restates correctly.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the figure line to 'p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s' (or 'SLO (p95) 2 s').

findings.evidence: "Fig 6.1's workload box therefore carries the request rate and the token profile; if the box displays a concurrency entry, read it as the request rate λ that the traffic offers, not as a concurrency value." (PDF 136). Drawn figure (PDF 137): "Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency".
findings.issue: Text asserts the workload box carries two items, but the drawn box displays three (including 'concurrency'); the declarative clause contradicts the figure while the trailing conditional concedes the third item — a figure-vs-text mismatch that invites misreading.
findings.fix_instruction: Align the text ("carries the request rate, the token profile and a concurrency entry that denotes λ") or remove 'concurrency' from the drawn workload box.

findings.evidence: Figure label: "Workload metrics rps · token profile · concurrency"; caption: "a concurrency entry in the workload box denotes the request rate λ that the traffic offers, not as a concurrency value — request concurrency is derived on the serving side (in-flight = λ × W, Little’s law)"
findings.issue: Figure 6.1 visually places "concurrency" in the workload-metrics box, while §6.1.1 and the caption explicitly state that concurrency is not a workload input and is derived on the serving side. The figure and its own caption use the same word for incompatible categories.
findings.fix_instruction: Remove "concurrency" from the workload box or relabel it as "arrival rate λ" / "offered request rate". If request concurrency is shown, move it to the serving/scheduler layer and reconcile §6.1.1, the figure, and the caption.
